panels.description: Wide, full page width. The mandapa of Padmanabhaswamy at night. Oil lamps in brass holders burn along every wall and pillar, their flames doubled in the polished stone floor until the whole hall seems to float on fire. Carved granite pillars recede into shadow. Beyond an open outer doorway, monsoon rain falls in a silver sheet. The nobles of Travancore stand packed in ranks, bare-chested in temple fashion, fine mundus and shoulder cloths, gold at their ears and throats catching the lamplight.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The monsoon of 1750, three days after Kottarakkara fell. The king called every noble in the kingdom to Padmanabhaswamy.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not for war council. Not for treaty.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some had lost kinsmen. Some had lost lands. All had learned to bow.

panels.description: The front ranks from behind and a little above. Nobles in order of importance, composed faces in profile, jewels glinting. In the front rank, one clear gap on the stone where no one stands, a single lamp's reflection lying in it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Near the front was the place where Padmini would once have stood, stick planted, eyes sharp.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Fever had taken her months before. The gap she left was as visible as any banner.

panels.description: Nagoji at the back of the hall among the lesser officers. He is Ananthan Pillai in temple dress: Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, NO turban, cream mundu, shoulder cloth over a bare chest, silver chain of office, no forehead marks, no sacred thread; strong cheekbones, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud. No coat inside the temple. Two nobles in the rank ahead glance back at him sidelong.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi had not come.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Her absence was noted, weighed, filed away.

panels.description: The temple attendant (young and slight, bare-chested, plain short mundu, hair in a small knot at the crown) lowers a great conch from his lips. A herald (middle-aged, bare-chested, white mundu, a plain staff of office) steps into the lamplight before the assembly, chin raised, voice trained to cut through drums and crowd. The herald and the attendant are NOT priests: do not use the temple-priest reference for either.

copy.speaker: HERALD
copy.text: Listen and witness.

copy.speaker: HERALD
copy.text: His Highness Sree Anizham Thirunal Marthanda Varma, Maharaja of Travancore.

copy.speaker: HERALD
copy.text: Victor of Colachel. Breaker of the Eight Houses.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. At the far doorway, Marthanda Varma enters. V13 varma-v1 face, aged: grey hair in a low knot, plain white mundu, bare torso with the sacred thread across his chest, no crown, no jewels, no headwear. He carries a sword flat across both palms, its hilt wrapped in silk, its blade catching the flames. Every head in the hall has turned.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had heard him called Varma, called Maharaja, called tiger.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Hearing the whole weight of him spoken aloud inside a temple made the air feel thinner.

panels.description: Low wide shot down the aisle of lamps. Varma (aged varma-v1 face, grey hair in a low knot, plain white mundu, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, no jewels) walks the length of the mandapa alone, small between the silent ranks, the sword across his palms. At the far end, before the sanctum, a row of temple priests chanting. The chief priest uses the V13 temple-priest face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The priests' chant was a river of sound. It had flowed here long before any of us were born.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It would flow long after we were dust.

panels.description: The threshold of the sanctum. Varma from behind, dwarfed, grey low knot and bare back. Through the doors, Lord Padmanabha reclining on the great serpent Anantha, seen only in fragments of gold and shadow: a vast shoulder, a resting hand, the many hoods of the serpent rising above. Draw it with reverence. The hoods seem to lean in the flicker of the lamps.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A thousand eyes, watching the one man who dared to stand before them.

panels.description: Full-width dark strip, about a third of the page tall, between 2.2 and 2.4. Beneath the flagged floor, a vault in blackness. Heaped coins and old chests catch a single thread of light in the centre of the strip: Roman gold, Venetian ducats, Dutch guilders, coins of empires long gone. Keep the left and right ends of the strip in deep black for the two captions, so the lettering never sits on the coins.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The true weight of this place was not in the stone. It was under it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The black gold of pepper, turned into the yellow gold of offerings. Enough to buy the Dutch East India Company three times over.

panels.description: Varma kneeling on the cold stone before the threshold, head bowed: grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, plain white mundu. Behind him the nobles are out of focus and utterly still. A lamp in the near foreground, its flame bending.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The silence was absolute. I could hear the hiss of oil in the nearest lamp.

panels.description: Tight, full-width strip. His hands lowering the sword to the stone, point toward the god, the silk-wrapped hilt touching down last.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It did not clatter. He laid it down the way a father lays down a sleeping child.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: One soft, final click.

panels.description: Varma still kneeling, face raised toward the sanctum, lit gold from within: aged varma-v1 face, grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, no jewels.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: From this day, I am no longer king of this land.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I am only the servant of He who lies here.

panels.description: Wide, from the back of the hall over the heads of the nobles. The kneeling figure is small and bright at the far end. His balloons reach all the way back to us.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: All that I have taken, all that I have built, all that I have paid for in blood and exile and broken houses...

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I give to Him. The kingdom is His. I merely hold it in trust.

panels.description: The priests raise their hands, the chant swelling. In the foreground, an old noble's face, eyes wet, lips moving in prayer.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The pious among them saw a king humbling himself before his god.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Others saw the trap.

panels.description: At the back of the hall, three men side by side facing the sanctum. Left foreground: Nagoji (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, bare chest, cream mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain of office clearly visible, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin), eyes forward on the sanctum. Centre: the whispering chief, a minor chief from the northern marches (heavy-set, older, shaven head with a small front tuft, heavy gold ear-rings, red-bordered shoulder cloth, grey stubble, no thick moustache), leaning right toward his neighbour, eyes wide, voice kept under the chant. Right: the neighbour (younger and thin, hair loose, plain shoulder cloth).

copy.speaker: CHIEF (whisper)
copy.text: He has given the land to god, so that he can keep it forever.

panels.description: The same three, closer on the chief and his neighbour. The neighbour (younger, thin, hair loose) lips twitching, not smiling. The chief (heavy-set, shaven head with a front tuft, gold ear-rings, red-bordered shoulder cloth) goes on, still leaning in. Nagoji's shoulder and silver chain at the left edge of frame.

copy.speaker: CHIEF (whisper)
copy.text: Who can take from a god what a god owns? Not Mysore. Not the Nizam. Not the Dutch.

copy.speaker: CHIEF (whisper)
copy.text: Not even a woman with a legitimate claim.

panels.description: Ramayyan Dalawa near the front, side-on to the sanctum: thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle under one arm. He is not watching the king and not watching the god. His eyes move along the bowed rows, lingering on a stiff shoulder here, a lifted chin there.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He was checking the mortar on this new wall they had built.

panels.description: Nagoji, close, lamplight across half his face (Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, bare shoulders, shoulder cloth, silver chain, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, no forehead marks), looking from Ramayyan to the kneeling king.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I understood then.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had built walls of stone and armies of men. Now he built a wall of faith, and it was the strongest of them all.

panels.description: Varma rising from his knees (grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, plain white mundu). The sword stays where he laid it at the threshold, drinking the lamplight. From the side, the temple attendant (young and slight, bare-chested, plain short mundu, hair in a small knot) steps forward carrying a bundle of thin coconut-leaf ribs. The nobles shift and turn to one another, lips moving behind raised hands.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But he was not finished.

panels.description: Inset, tight. A Kerala broom: a bundle of thin coconut-leaf ribs bound with coir at one end, no wooden pole, its tips worn ragged from honest work. It passes from the attendant's hands into the king's.

Full width, bottom. Varma bent low, one knee on the stone, sweeping before the sanctum with short, deliberate strokes of the handleless broom, gathering dust, scattered flower petals, ash from a thousand offerings: grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, plain white mundu. The nobles in the background frozen, their hands dropped, their mouths closed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The murmuring died. I could hear the bristles scraping on the stone.

panels.description: Large, top half of the page. High angle down the long pillared corridor that runs around the temple, lamps receding in two long lines. Far down it, one small bare-chested figure bent low over a short handleless broom of coconut-leaf ribs, mid-stroke. Nobles stand at the edges like statues. Past the outer wall, rain on the dark leaves of the serpent grove.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The king who had broken the Dutch, who had shattered the Eight Houses, who had built an army that made Mysore think twice.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Like any temple servant.

panels.description: Varma in the near foreground, down on his knees on the stone, sweeping with the short coconut-rib broom, his face lowered to the work (grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest). Behind him, standing among the nobles and watching him: the whispering chief from page 3 (heavy-set, shaven head with a small front tuft, heavy gold ear-rings, red-bordered shoulder cloth, grey stubble). The knowing look has gone out of the chief's face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: This was not theatre. This was a man who meant what he said.

panels.description: Back before the sanctum. Varma standing (grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest), his mundu grey with dust, his hands grey with ash. He hands the broom back to the temple attendant (young and slight, bare-chested, plain short mundu, hair in a small knot).

Nagoji's point of view across the hall. Varma has turned to face the assembly (grey hair in a low knot, bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, dust on his mundu), and his eyes have found Nagoji's.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: There was no triumph in his gaze. Only the weariness of a man who had finally placed his last piece on the board and could only wait to see if the game was won.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Row after row of nobles' heads going down across the mandapa. In the nearest bowing row, the whispering chief, his red-bordered shoulder cloth and shaven head readable. Beyond the bowing rows, Varma standing at the sanctum threshold and facing them (bare torso, sacred thread across his chest, grey low knot), the one head not bowed. The sword lies gleaming on the stone just behind his feet, at the god's threshold. The priests intone.

copy.speaker: PRIESTS
copy.text: Padmanabha Dasa.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Servant of Padmanabha.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The land belonged to god now.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: And god's servant still held the sword.

panels.description: Wide. A fort courtyard in early evening. Above the gate, the Travancore banner, a silver conch on red, lifting in the wind. Revathi Bayi stands alone on the flagstones looking up at it: deep indigo sari with gold, grey threading her black hair, jasmine in her braid, the tali on its yellow thread, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline. Behind her, in a doorway, Nagoji in uniform: white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, silver chain, sword at his hip; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: One week later.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That banner flew now over all the lands that had once been a dozen kingdoms.

panels.description: Two-shot. Revathi (indigo sari, jasmine braid, grey threading) still faces the banner, not him. Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban) has come a few steps into the courtyard.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: She reached Kochi. They gave her a small house. She tends a garden now.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am glad she lives.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Are you?

panels.description: Nagoji, silent, jaw set, the banner's shadow across him (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin). Her next balloon comes in from off-panel and lands on his face.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: You could have let her go. During the battle. You were close enough.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: She was trying to reach the boats.

panels.description: Revathi turns her head to him at last. No heat in her face, only weariness.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did not see her.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Liar.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Perhaps.

panels.description: Close on Revathi, looking at him as if seeing him for the first time. Nagoji soft in the background (white coat, topknot, NO turban).

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You have made your choice. Completely now. There is no more standing with one foot in each river.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You are his man. His sword. His builder.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Yes.

panels.description: Wide two-shot, a long stretch of flagstone between them. Revathi (indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, grey threading, tali) and Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban).

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And I am still hers. Her kinswoman. Her blood. The one who stood beside you in the same hall while you burned her claim.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Velinadu sent no men against us. You kept your doors closed.

panels.description: Revathi turning away a step, toward the gate, her face in profile against the evening light.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Closed is not the same as open.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Silence is not the same as support.

panels.description: She turns back.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: We will not be enemies. Velinadu and Travancore need each other too much for that.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: But we will never be simple. You chose. So did I.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: What did you choose?

panels.description: Tight on Revathi.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: To remember.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: When everyone else forgets what this cost, I will remember. Savitri's face. Her garden in Kochi. The laugh she will never laugh again.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Revathi walking out through the gate into the low gold evening, small, not looking back. Nagoji in the near foreground, still (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban), the banner above them both. Her last balloons trail back to him; his caption sits low beside him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Someone has to carry that weight. It will not be you. It will not be him.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: So it will be me.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Another world, where kings did not have to break houses to build kingdoms.

panels.description: Wide. Mavelikkara, 1753. A pavilion table. A Dutch East India Company commissioner in 1750s dress (knee-length skirted dark coat with wide turned-back cuffs, long waistcoat, knee breeches, white lace-edged stock, powdered bag-wig, his tricorn on the table) signs with a quill. Company soldiers in blue coats stand at the back. Across the table, Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) watches the pen, palm-leaf bundle at his elbow. No lettering on the document or on any flag.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Great Offering did what accounts and cannons could not.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Three years later the Dutch came back to Mavelikkara. This time they did not just bow.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They had sold their allies to save their trade.

panels.description: Night. A fort rampart, the stone still wet. Varma alone at the parapet, staring out at nothing: aged varma-v1 face, grey hair in a low knot, plain white mundu, a plain shoulder cloth over one shoulder, the sacred thread across his chest, no jewels, no headwear. Nagoji in uniform (white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud) coming along the wall walk toward him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: But the final cost of that peace was not written in ink.

panels.description: Varma, not turning, speaking to the dark.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The Nizam sent an envoy last month. Mysore's man was here before that.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The British build at Madras as if they mean to stay forever. And the Dutch, even now, count their losses and plan their next move.

panels.description: Varma turns to face Nagoji (aged varma-v1 face, grey hair in a low knot, plain shoulder cloth, sacred thread across his chest, no jewels).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: This is what I was always building toward. Not conquering for glory. Consolidating for survival.

panels.description: Over Varma's shoulder onto Nagoji, close, his face unreadable (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin). Varma's grey low knot and shoulder soft at the near edge of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Every house I absorbed, every chief I bent, every woman I exiled, it was all for this:

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: a kingdom strong enough that when they come, any of them, all of them, they will find more than pepper and prayers.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And the cost?

panels.description: Over Varma's shoulder (grey low knot, sacred thread, shoulder cloth) toward the dark: far off, the small lamps of distant forts on the hills. He is looking back out over the dark as he speaks.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The cost is that men like Savitri's kinsman die in rooms they cannot leave.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: That women like her tend gardens in foreign cities and curse my name.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: That Revathi looks at me like I am the disease I claimed to cure.

panels.description: Tight on his hands gripping the parapet, knuckles pale against the wet stone.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Do you think I do not feel it? Do you think I do not wake in the night and hear them?

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Every name. Every claim I denied. Every law I bent or broke.

panels.description: Varma's face, close, his voice cracking. Behind him, bleeding into the panel edge like a stain rather than a clean flashback frame: the same memory as the Chapter 27 stain (7.4), a sunlit courtyard long ago and young Savitri of Kottarakkara, a girl in her teens, her head thrown back in laughter. Her face is Savitri's Chapter 27 face made young. She wears a cream cloth with a red-and-gold border and simple gold at her ears and throat. NOT Revathi: no indigo, no jasmine braid, no tali, no flat-coin necklace.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I remember her laugh. From when we were young.

panels.description: Varma in profile against the night sky (grey low knot, sacred thread across his chest), his grip on the parapet loosening, one hand lying open on the wet stone. Nagoji small and out of focus behind him (white coat, topknot).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: And I remember the moment, in that tent, when I looked in her eyes and saw that she would never laugh again.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I did that. For this.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Wide over the rampart: the king's arm opening out toward the dark kingdom below, the lamps of forts on the far hills, the pale line of a road, the ordered cookfires of an army camp. Two small figures on the wall: Varma bare-chested in white, Nagoji in the white coat.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: For this.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had no comfort to offer.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some wounds are the price of building. Some prices are too high to name, but too necessary not to pay.

panels.description: Wide. Evening, a quiet corner of Udayagiri Fort. A small chapel of local stone with a simple wooden cross above its door. Through the open door: De Lannoy (tall, pale grey hair, clean-shaven, a worn white Travancore coat over a plain buff waistcoat, no red waistcoat) kneeling in the front pew with his head bowed; Father Duarte at a small altar, hands raised (thin, white-haired, scholar's stoop, plain black cassock with a small cross, NO white Roman collar tab, no stole or chasuble). Nagoji in uniform (white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, Kerala topknot, NO turban, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin) waits outside by the doorpost.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Udayagiri Fort. The Dutch had sailed away with their diminished pride.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Latin words that meant nothing to me, and everything to De Lannoy.

panels.description: De Lannoy (tall, pale grey hair, worn white coat, buff waistcoat) stepping out into the evening light, a peace in his face rarely seen in the war halls. Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban) at the doorpost, facing him.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Pillai. You do not usually visit this part of the fort.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I do not usually find two Europeans praying to their god in a kingdom that just surrendered itself to ours.

panels.description: Duarte in the doorway behind De Lannoy: the scholar's stoop, the ink-stained fingers, white hair, plain black cassock with a small cross, NO white Roman collar tab.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Father Duarte. I remembered those eyes from the dungeon. Now they held less guilt than acceptance.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: The Maharaja permits us this small space. We ask nothing of him but the right to serve.

panels.description: De Lannoy (worn white coat, buff waistcoat, pale grey hair) lays his palm flat on the chapel's stone doorframe as he speaks, the walls of the fort he designed rising behind him.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: And to pray. A man needs something beyond walls and accounts.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Otherwise the walls become a prison and the accounts become chains.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. The three of them at the foot of the fort wall in the low evening light, the chapel door behind them. Left to right: De Lannoy (worn white coat, buff waistcoat, tall, pale grey hair, clean-shaven), Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, topknot, NO turban, thick moustache), Duarte (white hair, plain black cassock, small cross, NO white Roman collar tab). As De Lannoy answers, Duarte steps forward out of the group toward Nagoji, his callused, ink-stained right hand just starting to lift.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: A Maratha cavalryman, a Dutch artillerist, a Portuguese priest.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Twenty years ago our peoples were killing each other across three continents. Now we stand under the same banner.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: The banner does not ask where we came from. Only where we stand now.

panels.description: Duarte's right hand, callused and ink-stained, stopped in the air between him and Nagoji, the black cassock sleeve fallen back from the wrist. Hold it. Nagoji (white coat, red waistcoat, topknot, NO turban) watching the hand. Duarte (white hair, plain black cassock, small cross, NO white Roman collar tab).
The hand completes the motion: a sign of the cross in Nagoji's direction, quick but deliberate. Duarte (white hair, plain black cassock, small cross, NO white Roman collar tab).

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: I do not do this to convert you. It is the only blessing I know how to give.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: And you have earned a blessing, Ananthan Pillai. Whatever you believe.

panels.description: A lighter beat. De Lannoy (worn white coat, buff waistcoat) half-smiling; Duarte (white hair, plain black cassock, NO white Roman collar tab) with the ghost of a smile.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: Even Ramayyan visited once. He spent the whole time examining the stonework rather than the altar.

copy.speaker: DUARTE
copy.text: He said the mortar was acceptable. High praise, from him.

panels.description: De Lannoy (tall, pale grey hair, worn white coat) looking back through the open chapel door at the floor before the altar. Quiet.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: When I die, I have asked to be buried here. In this fort I helped design. Under a stone that says I served Travancore.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. De Lannoy at left, his right hand gripping Nagoji's forearm; Nagoji at centre (white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, topknot, NO turban, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin); Duarte at right beside them (white hair, plain black cassock, small cross, NO white Roman collar tab). The fort wall behind, the evening sky above it.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: We are all servants now. You serve Padmanabha through the king. I serve Padmanabha through the walls.

copy.speaker: DE LANNOY
copy.text: It is a strange household. But it holds.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The kingdom had absorbed us all. And somehow, in the absorbing, it had made us more than we had been alone.

panels.description: Wide. A star-fort rampart at dusk, monsoon clouds building over the sea. Nagoji old now, on the nagoji-v2 later-life sheet: grey-streaked hair in a topknot, white mundu with a gold border, its end draped over one shoulder, no coat, NO turban, the same thick curled moustache and clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, leaning on the parapet. Beside him a young Travancore officer: about twenty, round-faced, slighter than Nagoji, clean-shaven with no moustache, no ear stud, hair in a small Nair tuft at the crown, in a white European-cut coat and red waistcoat. The officer is NOT Nagoji: do not use the Nagoji reference for him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Years later, when my joints ached with old battles.

copy.speaker: OFFICER
copy.text: What was Travancore like, before it was Travancore?

panels.description: Inset. Remembered: the map on the war-hall table, a painted map of the south of the peninsula with the sea to the left. Colour regions: red inland to the north (Mysore), black far to the north (the Nizam), brown to the east (Arcot), small blue marks at the coastal forts (the Europeans), and many small pale patches crowded along the south-west coast. No place names, labels or lettering anywhere on the map.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: When I first washed ashore, the king borrowed lancers from Madurai and begged muskets from English factors. His horses feared the sand.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Now there were fifty thousand men under arms. All of it paid for in pepper and blood.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I miss what it cost.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He had been born into the kingdom we built. He did not know what had been burned to make it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (faded)
copy.text: He seems to favour whoever has the better powder.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That young man had been wrong. Belief had turned out to matter more than anything.

copy.speaker: CAPTION

copy.text: One night on her western verandah, long before Savitri's banners rose, I almost told her I would lay down my marches if she asked.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The words sat on my tongue like a loaded musket.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Perhaps that mercy was hers, not mine.

panels.description: Wide, split down the middle, the same rain falling across both halves. Left: a small garden in Kochi, Savitri elderly, in white, lines of care, among her plants; no jasmine, no indigo. copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The monsoon came that year, as it always did.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (tag, left half)
copy.text: Kochi.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (tag, right half)
copy.text: Velinadu.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (right half)
copy.text: She remembered. The children in the rain carried my blood and hers.

panels.description: Large, bottom half of the page. copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Here I stood guard over what we had built from the ashes of what they had lost.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That was the price. That was always the price.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some things do not wash.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some things we carry.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: For as long as we live, and in the stories that outlast us.
